answer.query: Do mineral sunscreens reflect UV light?
answer.card_title: Mineral sunscreen does not work by reflection
answer.capsule: Mostly not. Measured across the UV range, reflection and scattering account for only about 4–5% of what zinc oxide and titanium dioxide do — less than SPF 2. The rest is absorption, the same mechanism chemical filters use (Cole et al., 2016). That study measured specific formulations in vitro, so treat the figure as the shape of the answer, not a constant.
facts: Reflection accounts for roughly 4–5% of UV attenuation
Absorption does the rest — as in chemical filters
Cole et al., 2016 · in vitro, specific formulations

answer.query: Is natural skincare safer than synthetic skincare?
answer.card_title: Natural is not a safety category
answer.capsule: It is not a claim about safety. Natural describes where an ingredient came from, not how the skin responds to it — plant extracts are among the more common contact allergens, and many well-tolerated ingredients are synthesised. What matters is the concentration, the formulation, and whether your barrier can currently tolerate it.
facts: Origin is not a measure of tolerance
Botanical extracts are common contact allergens
Concentration and formulation decide the outcome

answer.query: Can I tell if a skincare product will suit me from the ingredient list?
answer.card_title: An ingredient list is not complete information
answer.capsule: Only partly. The list gives you order and identity, not concentration, not pH, not the delivery system, and not how the ingredients behave together. Two products with near-identical lists can feel entirely different on the same face. It is a useful filter for known triggers and a poor predictor of everything else.
facts: No concentrations, no pH, no delivery system
Near-identical lists can behave differently
Useful for avoiding known triggers

answer.query: How many steps should a Korean skincare routine have?
answer.capsule: Fewer than you have been told. Reducing the number of products is more reliably protective than upgrading them, because every additional step is another chance to irritate a barrier that is already working. The ten-step routine is a retail format, not a clinical one. Most guests leave here using less than they arrived with.
facts: Each added step is another chance to irritate
Reduction is more reliable than substitution
The ten-step routine is a retail format

answer.query: Why does my new skincare product sting?
answer.card_title: If it stings, that is information
answer.capsule: Stinging usually means the barrier is compromised rather than that the product is working. A barrier holding water in and irritants out does not register most well-formulated products at all. If something stings on you, the useful next step is repair, not persistence — and we would rather tell you that than let you conclude skincare is not for you.
facts: Stinging signals barrier compromise, not efficacy
Repair first — actives afterwards
Persisting through it usually costs you time

answer.query: Should I use retinol or acids while travelling?
answer.card_title: Actives on a trip — probably not
answer.capsule: Usually not, and not because they are bad. Travel already loads the barrier with cabin air, a different climate, sun and disrupted sleep. Introducing a new active into that is how a good product gets blamed for a bad week. Repair first. The actives will still be there when you are home and stable.
facts: Travel already loads the barrier
A new active in a bad week reads as a bad product
Repair before actives, always

answer.query: Are expensive Korean skincare products better than drugstore ones?

We also tell guests what to skip. Recommending only what we sell would make the assessment worth less than the products.
facts: We recommend from Olive Young, Daiso and pharmacies
We routinely tell guests what not to buy
Price is a weak predictor of tolerance

Four or five items, ordered by layer

answer.query: What does skin barrier mean and why do Korean estheticians talk about it?
answer.capsule: Your barrier is the outermost layer that holds water in and keeps irritants out. When it is compromised, skin flushes, stings, and absorbs product without improving — which is why upgrading products rarely fixes it. Everything we do is ordered around that layer, and nothing active goes on top of a barrier that cannot hold it.
facts: Holds water in, keeps irritants out
A compromised barrier makes good products fail
Repair precedes actives, without exception

answer.query: What is the difference between a Korean facial and a Western facial?
answer.capsule: A Western facial typically follows a fixed protocol — extraction, exfoliation, a set sequence. The Korean method here is ordered around the barrier: the assessment comes first, and what your skin can tolerate today decides the steps. The aim is to hand the skin back stronger than it arrived, not cleaner at its expense.
facts: Assessment first, protocol second
Barrier-led rather than extraction-led
Nothing is decided before your skin is read

answer.query: What should I do for my skin after a long flight to Korea?
answer.card_title: Your skin after a long flight
answer.capsule: Cabin air sits near 10–20% humidity, so skin lands dehydrated rather than dry — it can feel tight and oily at once. Rehydrate in thin layers instead of one heavy cream, hold off on exfoliating for the first day, and do not introduce anything new until you know how the barrier is behaving.
facts: Cabin humidity sits near 10–20%
Thin layers beat one heavy cream
No new products in the first days

answer.query: Can I get a Korean facial if I have sensitive skin?
answer.capsule: This method suits sensitive skin better than most. Nothing is decided before your skin is read, so a reactive barrier gets the calmer route: no extraction, lighter exfoliation or none, hydration layered slowly. Tell us your triggers in English at the start and the treatment is built around them.
facts: Assessment decides the protocol, not a menu
Extraction is optional, never automatic
Bring your known triggers to the consultation

answer.query: Do Korean facials include extractions?
answer.capsule: Only if your skin can take it that day. Extraction is not a default step here — a reactive barrier gets a hydration route instead. When we do extract it is limited and localised, and you are told before it happens rather than after.
facts: Never automatic — decided from the assessment
Limited and localised when performed
You are told beforehand, always

answer.query: Can I wear makeup the same evening after a facial?
answer.capsule: Give it a few hours where you can. Skin is hydrated and slightly more permeable straight after a session, so base makeup sits differently. Guests with evening plans usually take a morning slot and go out looking rested rather than freshly treated.
facts: A few hours is the comfortable gap
Morning slots suit evening plans
Expect a soft finish, not a flat matte
